consumer_adoption: The Home renderer must consume read-deal-update-reviews and render this new proposal kind. This backend contract does not change the existing app renderer.

record.judgment: One bounded Jev systemOne call covers the calling partner's overdue ordinary and accepted post-call actions. Structured checklist items and other partners' actions remain separate.
record.automatic_resolution: yes, confidence at least 0.9, valid choice distribution, and the shared #2449 evidence bar including four quoted words. The 0.9 numeric threshold is additional to #2449's deterministic evidence bar.
record.evidence: Each immutable overdue_assessment event retains the action snapshot, note ID, complete update, exact selected quote, verdict, confidence, reason, and completion stamp.
record.failure: Missing credentials, provider errors, rate limits, time budget and input bounds preserve the open item and record a reason.
record.plan: A supplied next_step and next_date are saved together. The app's separate set-next-step command also preserves previously assessed unresolved overdue actions. Without a new plan, a resolved current action clears the obsolete plan and prompts for its replacement.

read.membership: Latest uncertain or low-confidence assessment for an open action, visible in the authenticated actor's tenant and personal scope, not already reviewed.
read.limit: Above 200 pending proposals the read refuses instead of silently truncating.
read.automatic_resolution_membership: Automatic resolutions from the last seven days for actions owned by the caller, excluding reviewed assessments. undo_possible reflects whether the coupled actions and plan remain unchanged.

decisions.resolve: Complete the exact unchanged action after partner review.
decisions.dismiss: Remove the proposal while leaving its action open.
decisions.undo: Reopen an unchanged automatic completion and reverse its coupled plan while no newer plan change exists.

review.replay: Retry with the original key. A changed action or newer plan refuses rather than overwriting subsequent work.
